svg.title: When Self-Hypnosis Gets Intense — updated safety map

text.tspan: Stabilize before interpreting. Capacity before content. Commune with love and boundaries.
Images, sensations, or signals may be meaningful —
but they are hypotheses, not proof.
Ask what is fake: wording, image,
There may be no answer. Change the question,
Skepticism may be reasonable. Hear it
Check body, environment, and actual danger
first; if a protective concern is
Ask: “What happens to ordinary life after this?”
More clarity/action — or more repetition, craving,
and avoidance? What real action, if any, is inside this?
Return fully: body, room, movement, eyes
One grounded action / outside help as
A meaningful experience is not the same thing as a verified ontology.
Do not use self-hypnosis while driving, bathing, swimming,
operating equipment, or supervising someone who needs
Do not force memory recovery or use trance to prove what
Do not treat inner voices, images, autonomous movements, or
body signals as commands or proof.
Do not override hunger, fatigue, pain, grief, anger, or fear
Do not prolong altered states indefinitely or treat intuition
Do not let the child, Protector, guide, or narrator replace
Do not deepen when reality-testing, sleep, or ordinary
End every waking session with ordinary identity, movement,
orientation, judgment, eyes open, and a direct statement that
• Immediate danger or inability to keep yourself safe.
• Chest pain, fainting, seizure, possible overdose, severe confusion, or
• New/worsening suicidal thoughts; severe insomnia; mania-like or
• Dissociation or paranoia that disrupts functioning.
• Recurring panic, compulsive behavior, substance destabilization, or
• Trauma regression / unknown-origin searching: use a trained clinician.
• Shorter sessions, manageable subject, full return, one target at a time.
• If function worsens or unverifiable memories feel increasingly certain:
“Stabilize. Orient. Listen only if useful. Return. Integrate.”
